The DOMINANT remaining cost in real 871 is not opcode structure at all but a SCHEDULE difference repeated across the ~13 SWAP32 expansions: MWCC software-pipelines our byte-copy chain across TWO registers (r0 and r3/r6/r7), hoisting each lbz ahead of the previous stb, whereas the target emits a strict single-register r0 lbz/stb alternation. Opcodes and counts are identical in those regions; only register count and ordering differ. The union frame order was corrected this session (target has _s BELOW _d; ours had them reversed until the declaration order was swapped), so the layout premise for that schedule is now aligned and the residual is reduced to the allocator's willingness to spend a second scratch register. The SWAP32/SWAP16/SWAPF32 macros are used by NO other function in the TU (all 40 uses are inside fn_8001267C; fn_80011DCC uses the separate AtreeNodeSwap32 helper and AtreeInitSub uses neither), so the macro shape remains free to reshape for a future pass without endangering the exact sibling or the pinned function.
